es.summary: Daño al parénquima hepático causado por la toxicidad directa o inmunomediada de medicamentos.
key_points: La LHI se presenta con elevación aguda de ALT/AST > 3 veces el límite superior normal.
Los antibióticos, anticonvulsivantes, estatinas y paracetamol son causas frecuentes.
El diagnóstico se basa en historia de exposición, pruebas de función hepática y exclusión de otras causas.
El manejo principal es la interrupción del fármaco y soporte hepático.

pathophysiology: El fármaco se metaboliza en el hepatocito generando metabolitos reactivos.
Los metabolitos pueden dañar membranas celulares y proteínas, provocando necrosis o apoptosis.
En algunos casos se desencadena una respuesta inmunitaria que agrava la lesión.
La lesión reduce la capacidad de síntesis de proteínas y detoxificación.
risk_factors: Uso de dosis altas o prolongadas de paracetamol.
Polifarmacia, especialmente con antibióticos, anticonvulsivantes y estatinas.
signs_symptoms: Ictericia (ictericia amarilla de piel y escleras).
diagnostics: ALT y AST elevados > 3‑5× límite superior normal (U/L).
Bilirrubina total > 2 mg/dL y bilirrubina directa aumentada.
INR > 1.5 indica compromiso de síntesis de factores de coagulación.
Ecografía hepática para descartar obstrucción biliar.
treatment: Corticosteroides en LHI inmunomediada (ej. por antibióticos).
Soporte hemodinámico y manejo de complicaciones (ej. encefalopatía).
complications: Ascitis y edema por hipertensión portal.
nursing_care: Monitorear LFTs (ALT, AST, bilirrubina) cada 24‑48 h.
Evaluar signos de sangrado: petequias, sangrado gingival.
Controlar estado mental y nivel de conciencia.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; vigilar edema y ascitis.
patient_teaching: Informar sobre la necesidad de evitar el fármaco y notificar cualquier nuevo medicamento.
Evitar alcohol y sustancias hepatotóxicas mientras se recupera.
Reconocer signos de ictericia, dolor abdominal y confusión; buscar atención inmediata.
Seguir dieta baja en grasas y mantener hidratación adecuada.

outcomes: Función hepática: ALT y AST dentro de rango normal en 7‑10 días.
Conocimiento: paciente identifica al menos tres signos de lesión hepática.

interventions.action: Revisar la lista de medicamentos y notificar al médico sobre posibles hepatotóxicos.
interventions.rationale: Previene la exposición continua a agentes causantes.

interventions.action: Monitorear LFTs y coagulación cada 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Detecta deterioro temprano y guía intervenciones.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de sangrado y registrar cualquier petequia o hemorragia.
interventions.rationale: La lesión hepática afecta la síntesis de factores de coagulación.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de evitar alcohol y automedicación.
interventions.rationale: Reduce factores de riesgo adicionales para el hígado.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Balance hídrico: I&O registrado y equilibrado en 48 h.
Edema: reducción visible del edema periférico en 72 h.

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y eliminación de líquidos cada 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar retención o déficit de líquidos.

interventions.action: Evaluar peso diario y comparar con peso basal.
interventions.rationale: Cambio de peso indica acumulación o pérdida de líquidos.

interventions.action: Observar y medir circunferencia de abdomen para detectar ascitis.
interventions.rationale: Ascitis es signo de retención de líquidos en insuficiencia hepática.

interventions.action: Administrar diuréticos según indicación médica y monitorizar respuesta.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la eliminación de exceso de líquido y previene sobrecarga.

interventions.action: Mantener al paciente en posición semisentado para facilitar la respiración y reducir presión abdominal.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la ventilación y disminuye la sensación de plenitud.

en.summary: Damage to hepatic parenchyma caused by direct or immune-mediated toxicity of medications.
key_points: DILI presents with an acute rise in ALT/AST > 3 times the upper limit of normal.
Antibiotics, anticonvulsants, statins, and acetaminophen are common causes.
Diagnosis is based on exposure history, liver function tests, and exclusion of other causes.
The main management is discontinuation of the drug and hepatic support.

pathophysiology: The drug is metabolized in the hepatocyte producing reactive metabolites.
Metabolites can damage cell membranes and proteins, causing necrosis or apoptosis.
In some cases an immune response is triggered, worsening the injury.
The injury reduces protein synthesis and detoxification capacity.
risk_factors: High or prolonged doses of acetaminophen.
Polypharmacy, especially with antibiotics, anticonvulsants, and statins.
diagnostics: ALT and AST > 3‑5× upper limit of normal (U/L).
Total bilirubin > 2 mg/dL and direct bilirubin increased.
INR > 1.5 indicates impaired coagulation factor synthesis.
Abdominal ultrasound to rule out biliary obstruction.
treatment: Corticosteroids for immune-mediated DILI (e.g., due to antibiotics).
Hemodynamic support and management of complications (e.g., encephalopathy).
complications: Ascites and edema due to portal hypertension.
nursing_care: Monitor LFTs (ALT, AST, bilirubin) every 24‑48 h.
Assess for bleeding signs: petechiae, gingival bleeding.
Monitor mental status and level of consciousness.
Record intake and output; monitor for edema and ascites.
patient_teaching: Inform about the need to avoid the drug and report any new medication.
Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic substances while recovering.
Recognize signs of jaundice, abdominal pain, and confusion; seek immediate care.
Follow a low-fat diet and maintain adequate hydration.

outcomes: Liver function: ALT and AST within normal range in 7‑10 days.
Knowledge: patient identifies at least three signs of liver injury.

interventions.action: Review the medication list and notify the physician of potential hepatotoxins.
interventions.rationale: Prevents continued exposure to causative agents.

interventions.action: Monitor LFTs and coagulation every 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Detects early deterioration and guides interventions.

interventions.action: Assess for bleeding signs and record any petechiae or hemorrhage.
interventions.rationale: Liver injury affects coagulation factor synthesis.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of avoiding alcohol and self-medication.
interventions.rationale: Reduces additional risk factors for the liver.

outcomes: Fluid balance: I&O recorded and balanced in 48 h.
Edema: visible reduction of peripheral edema in 72 h.

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Allows detection of fluid retention or deficit.

interventions.action: Assess daily weight and compare to baseline weight.
interventions.rationale: Weight change indicates fluid accumulation or loss.

interventions.action: Observe and measure abdominal circumference to detect ascites.
interventions.rationale: Ascites is a sign of fluid retention in hepatic failure.

interventions.action: Administer diuretics as ordered and monitor response.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates removal of excess fluid and prevents overload.

interventions.action: Keep the patient in a semi‑upright position to aid breathing and reduce abdominal pressure.
interventions.rationale: Improves ventilation and decreases fullness sensation.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Jaundice occurs when skin and sclera (whites of the eyes) ( Figure 19.17 ) turn yellow as a result of too much bilirubin in the body.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Symptoms can include sudden severe pain in the right upper abdomen, nausea, and vomiting.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Occur approximately 40 days after exposure; include anorexia nausea vomiting abdominal pain jaundice

sections.complications.2.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.3.quote: Common complications seen with chronic liver disease are esophageal varices , hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome (kidney dysfunction in patients with advanced liver disease), and hepatocellular carcinoma.
